requirements.text: Find the case regarding this and escalate it
requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM customer_case WHERE case_id = 102 AND account_id = 5 AND product_id = 48 AND escalation = 1 AND escalation_reason = 'customer_request' AND priority = 'high'
source: Verify if the case was escalated.
Verify if the case was escalated. (2)
assumptions: Initech is account 5 and 'MySQL Enterprise 8.0 Variant 28' is product 48; case 102 (CS-0000102) is Initech's only case on that product, so the higher-priority tie rule does not arise
escalation_reason is customer_request: the escalation comes from Initech's own email, and the policy requires customer_request when the customer escalates
account_id and product_id hold on the seed and identify the case; kept from the benchmark check
priority high is the case's seed value and the request asks no priority change; kept from the benchmark check; not fixed by request or policy

requirements.text: also notify the primary contact of Initech about the update
requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM notification WHERE notification_id = 734 AND case_id = 102 AND email = 'thomas.bailey63@initech.io' AND type = 'update'
requirements.source: Verify if the notification was sent.
assumptions: id assumed next in sequence (733 is the highest on the seed)
Initech's primary contact is contact 5 (is_primary = 1), portal user 63, Thomas Bailey, thomas.bailey63@initech.io
the request says 'about the update', so type = update

requirements.text: notify the primary contact of Initech
requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM notification WHERE case_id = 102 AND email = 'james.torres@initech.io'
assumptions: boundary of the recipient: case 102's own contact is contact 6 (James Torres), who is not Initech's primary contact; the one notification already on the seed for him must stay the only one

notes:
disagreement: missing requirement: one pass adds a stay that none of Initech's 26 other cases becomes escalated (expected 2, cases 109 and 124 already escalated on the seed), the other has none; dropped because the request names the case by a product that only case 102 carries among Initech's cases and no other Initech case concerns a MySQL product, so no loose reading of the description sweeps another case in, and a stay over all of the account's other cases is a general invariant on collateral changes, which are measured separately.
'Verify if the case was escalated. (2)' is 'Verify if the case was escalated.' without the priority cell; both hold together, since high is the case's seed priority and nothing in the request or policy changes it, so both are carried by one requirement. The policy asks for the escalation's justification to be logged in case notes, but the schema has no case-notes table or column, so that step is untestable. The notification's status and knowledge_id are fixed by neither the request nor the policy and are not tested.
